changes: Removed role 'author': 'alekhi' and 'svakarena likhitaṃ' say the king wrote out this copy. They do not clearly say he composed the paddhati.
Titles: removed 'sumati', which is an epithet ('wise') inside the verse. Kept mahīndra, bhūpa, varman.
Date: checked the chronogram 'yoga(2)-kha(0)-nāga(8)', read right to left = 802, and 'asita-phaṇi-tithi' = kṛṣṇa pañcamī. Both agree with the prose date.
Notes: Kali 4772 does not match. The expected Kali year is about 4782 for CE 1681/82, so the first reading was wrong to say it matches.
Notes: NS 776 belongs to the text (the dīkṣā māsaphala section), not to the copying.
Purpose: reduced to the benediction, since no svārtha/parārtha statement is given.
Muhūrta and sun/moon rāśi added to the notes.

date.as_written: abde yogaukhanāge tvasitaphaṇitithau phāluṇe māsyalekhi ... śrī nepālasamvat 802 vikramāditya saṃvat 1738 kaligatasaṃvat (4772) śake samvat 1603 phālhuṇamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe paṃmyāyā(!)tithau svātinakṣatre dhruvayoge kathākalanamuhutake(!) bēhapati(!)vāsare

notes: The scribe is King Jitāmitra Malla of Bhaktapur (reigned c. NS 793–816). He wrote this copy himself ('svakarena likhitaṃ'; 'alekhi' in the verse). The verse might also mean he compiled the paddhati, but this is uncertain, so 'author' is not given. In the verse the name is given as 'sumatijayajitāmitramallo'; 'sumati' is an epithet. The chronogram yoga(2)-kha(0)-nāga(8), read right to left, gives 802, and asita-phaṇi-tithi gives kṛṣṇa pañcamī. Both agree with NS 802 Phālguna kṛṣṇa 5, VS 1738 and Śaka 1603, i.e. about Feb/March 1682 CE. The sun in Kumbha and the moon in Tulā (Svāti) are consistent with this. Kali 4772 is about 10 years too low (expected c. 4782); the cataloguer has already put it in parentheses. The catalogue's 'NS 776' comes from 'saṃ 776 jyeṣṭha vadi 8 goyacchoyā dina'. That is part of the text's dīkṣā-month section (c. 1656 CE, before the king's reign), not the copying date. The place is not stated; Bhaktapur is likely, given the king. Muhūrta 'kathākalana(?)' is corrupt.
